newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends firm, funds buy 75 million bushels.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends firm, funds buy 75 million bushels.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed firmer on Wednesday as commodity funds continued their aggressive buying pattern, accounting for an estimated 75 million bushels in corn purchases on the day, traders said.
Profit taking by local traders trimmed gains late.
"The funds are making a move out of the shorts and they're going long," a floor trader said.

Funds had bought an estimated 100 million bushels of corn during Tuesday's session. Open interest jumped by 100 million bushels on Tuesday, CBOT said. Floor traders said it was the largest single-day gain in recent memory.

New crop December led the surge on Wednesday on ideas recent gains in soybeans would tempt farmers to plant soybeans instead of corn. Traders said the market needed to "buy back" corn acreage from soybeans by raising new crop prices.
Corn had opened weak on commercial hedging tied to farmer selling. Cash sources noted active farmer selling on Tuesday after March corn jumped 8-3/4 cents a bushel to $2.82-3/4.
But selling interest waned on Wednesday and commercials were buyers in early trade, floor sources said.
Corn ended 2-3/4 to 3/4 cent per bushel higher with March up 3/4 at $2.83-1/2 and December up 1-1/4 at $2.76.

On the day, Cargill Inc bought eight million bushels May and two million July and sold two million May and one million each March and July. ADM bought two million May but sold three million May and 1.5 million March.

Refco Inc bought 10 million bushels May, eight million March and three million December. Griffin Trading and LIT each bought five million July and Smith Barney bought six million July and two million May.

In options trade, Tenco Inc bought 1,000 May $2.90 calls and 7-1/2 cents and sold 1,000 May $3.00 calls at 4-3/4 to five cents. ABN-Chicago Corporation bought 1,000 December $3.00 calls at 11-3/4 to 12-1/2 cents, traders said.
Prudential Securities bought 2,000 March $2.90 calls at 1-1/2 to 1-5/8 cents.
Technical traders said moving average signals were bullish. Resistance Thursday was pegged at $2.88 per bushel in the March with support at $2.80-1/4.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 120,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's volume of 143,338 contracts.
